messages:
alex: quick proposal for handling noisy upstreams during streaming — looking for design feedback. idea in 1 sentence: soft-shape by detecting lack-of-progress, checkpoint the KV/token window, then failover to a standby upstream with resume headers so clients see a continuous stream rather than a hard error. PTAL.

alex: rationale: we've seen a few customer incidents where an upstream stalls mid-stream (network flaps, GC spikes). current behavior is either long tail latency or an immediate hard abort. both are bad for UX and SLOs. soft-failover could reduce visible failures while keeping costs reasonable.

jenny: can you define "lack-of-progress" precisely? is it bytes/time or model-token-output? we need a metric we can measure cheaply.

alex: good q. practical version: progress = downstream-ack of bytes OR upstream write progress observed by proxy. impl we discussed: maintain per-stream last-progress-ts; if no progress for X ms (configurable) and stream is still open, mark as 'stalled'. default X=2000ms for short-response models, larger for long-tail convs.

kai: big concern: duplication/side-effects. if we reconnect and the model resumes, we must avoid double-executing stateful tools or billing duplicates. we need an idempotency token and resume-offset semantics. suggest headers:

```
X-Resume-Id: <uuid>        # unique per client-request
X-Resume-Offset: <token-index>  # last confirmed token index client saw
X-Resume-Mode: guarded | blind   # guarded = server must ensure no duplicate side-effects
```

kai: also need server-side guarantee that resume succeeds only if the replacement upstream supports the same model variant or a compatible fallback.

alex: +1 on headers. implementation note: we won't rewind the model — instead we provide cached prefix/KV (if available) to the secondary and set generation offset so tokens already delivered aren't re-sent. if exact prefix not available, fallback policy: either synthesize partial trailer "incomplete-resume" or choose smaller model that can reconstruct context.

infra-bot: staging run summary (last 24h): 120k streaming sessions, hedged ~2.1% after 2s stall threshold. p99 latency reduced from 2.7s -> 2.2s for affected routes. memory overhead +7% at edge-proxy (KV cache + checkpoint meta). failure injections: 90% success on resume handshakes, 10% ended in partial-trailer.

samir: those numbers look promising, but what's the SLO accounting? if we resume on secondary with lower-quality model, how do we reflect that in SLIs/alerts?

maria: proposal: add per-response quality tag in trace/metrics (response.quality = exact | downgraded | partial-resume). hook this into Optimize so customers get alerted on quality regressions separate from latency. also surface sampled transcripts for debugging.

jenny: operation complexity: do we allow automatic hedging across regions? cross-region failover reduces stall but costs more and may violate data residency. we need policy flags: allow_hedge_regions: true/false per-tenant.

alex: agreed. default to same-region only, enterprise can opt-in for cross-region. also require KMS policy for any cross-region resume since we may transfer old KV metadata.

kai: test matrix we need before RFC: unit tests for resume-header parsing, integration test with simulated upstream stall + KV warm/cold, chaos test for duplicate token suppression, and billing audit to ensure no double-charge.

jenny: I'll own the RFC follow-up with state machine sketch and integration test plan. will add a compact timeline for canary.

alex: thanks. tentative rollout plan: canary 10% on vip-edge-2, measure p99, resume-success-rate, memory delta; then ramp 25/50/100 with kill-switch.

deploy-bot: canary started on vip-edge-2 (10% traffic) — run id 2026-03-20T09:14Z.

maria: one more thought — adaptive threshold: instead of fixed 2s, compute stall-window = max(2000ms, 2 * median_inter_token_time_for_stream). reduces false-positives for slow-long streams.

samir: +1 to adaptive. also add a backoff so we don't re-hedge repeatedly on the same stream.

alex: action items: alex -> draft RFC + state machine; jenny -> test matrix + perf harness; kai -> resume header draft + idempotency checklist; maria -> metric/trace tags and Optimize integration. I'll post RFC in #architecture by EOD and schedule a follow-up sync if needed. :thumbsup:
